results.edit: pin_extension() raises the cap whatever the ledger's claim log holds
results.why_it_matters: an extension approved for one ledger would raise the cap of any ledger at the root

results.edit: _limits() ignores the pinned extension
results.why_it_matters: the approval would be read and pinned and still grant nothing

results.edit: _limits() adds the extension's limits twice
results.why_it_matters: more requests than the owner approved

results.edit: reclaim_ordinal() allows a URL requested under the extension to be requested again
results.why_it_matters: zero automatic retries would become one retry per pass

results.edit: reclaim_ordinal() ignores why the planner asks again
results.why_it_matters: a failed first request of a named class would be retried without being a replacement

results.edit: reclaim_ordinal() ignores which classes the owner named
results.why_it_matters: a refresh of a class the owner did not name would be requested again

results.edit: _capture_one() takes a re-request marker from a caller with no extension
results.why_it_matters: a claimed URL could be requested again by anything that passes the marker

results.edit: _capture_one() requests again with the first request's exact bytes
results.why_it_matters: the same digest twice is the redraw the ledger forbids; the replacement could never be made

results.edit: extended_allowance() keeps the first approval's grants
results.why_it_matters: requests after the extension would be held to grants the owner did not approve for them

results.edit: _approved_body() does not compare the comment with the policy
results.why_it_matters: a policy file could grant more than the owner's comment says

results.edit: _typed() does not tie the extension to the approval it names
results.why_it_matters: an extension of another approval would raise this one's cap

results.edit: _approved_body() fetches the comment and does not compare it with the saved record
results.why_it_matters: a locally written record would stand for an approval nobody posted

results.edit: lost_segment_reserve() counts every claimed URL as done
results.why_it_matters: a lost host may have requested it again under the extension; the charge would miss it

results.edit: _extension() records an extension beside an approval it does not extend
results.why_it_matters: the branch would say a ledger was spent under an extension of another approval

results.edit: live_ledger() reads the extension and does not pin it
results.why_it_matters: production would stop at the first cap while every recorded case passed

results.edit: reclaim_ordinal() requests again any copy the planner cannot read
results.why_it_matters: a changed hash or a conflicting attempt is not the failed request the owner named (review L2)

results.edit: _capture_one() takes the marker it is handed without reading the slots
results.why_it_matters: a URL already requested under the extension could be requested a third time (review L3)

results.edit: pin_extension() does not compare the stated spending with the claim log
results.why_it_matters: the owner could approve an increment against a spending that was not the ledger's (review L4)

results.edit: pin_extension() accepts an extension other than the one first pinned at the root
results.why_it_matters: an unverified dict could raise the cap after the real extension was pinned (review L1)

results.edit: live_ledger() pins an extension that was not read back from GitHub
results.why_it_matters: a locally written extension would raise the live cap (review L1)

results.edit: _check() lets a session hold other grants than its ledger's extension
results.why_it_matters: requests would be counted against one approval and admitted by another (review L1, the uncaught injection)

results.edit: live_historical_session() does not compare the extension with the branch tip
results.why_it_matters: an extension never pushed could be spent, and a resume reading the branch could not charge for it (review M1)

results.edit: require_extension_on_branch() accepts files the branch does not carry
results.why_it_matters: the same as above, inside the check itself (review M1)

results.edit: resume_ledger() charges an export spent under an extension without it
results.why_it_matters: the lost segment's charge would leave out the rows only the extension admits (review M1)

results.edit: require_published_resume() keeps a resume charged under another extension
results.why_it_matters: its reserve was not computed against the grants now spent (review M1)

results.edit: resume_reserve_at_state() counts every resume in the chain as spent at the state
results.why_it_matters: a resume after the state, restoring the stated export, would refuse every later pin (the re-review's N1)

results.edit: resume_reserve_at_state() lets a resume that restored an earlier log sit outside the stated chain
results.why_it_matters: the stated spending would understate a charge made before the state

results.edit: resume_reserve_at_state() does not compare the chain with the stated bytes
results.why_it_matters: a chain whose charges were changed after the state would be read as the stated one
